This document defines expected employee behavior, prohibited conduct,
and the disciplinary process for violations.

- Prohibited conduct includes: harassment or discrimination of any kind,
falsification of company records (including expense reports - see
Expense Reimbursement Policy), unauthorized disclosure of confidential
information, and misuse of company systems (see IT & Security Policy).
- Violations are classified into three severity tiers:
- **Minor** (e.g. repeated lateness, dress code violations): verbal
warning, documented in the employee's file.
- **Moderate** (e.g. policy violations, insubordination): written
warning and a formal improvement plan.
- **Severe** (e.g. harassment, theft, falsification of records):
immediate suspension pending investigation, up to and including
termination.
- Employees have the right to have a peer or HR representative present
during any disciplinary meeting related to a Moderate or Severe
violation.
- All reports of misconduct are handled confidentially by HR, and
retaliation against an employee who files a report in good faith is
itself classified as a Severe violation.

- A Minor violation does not escalate to Moderate automatically, unless
three or more Minor violations occur within a rolling 6-month period,
in which case the fourth is treated as Moderate regardless of its
individual severity.
- Conduct occurring outside of work hours or company premises may still
be subject to this policy if it directly affects the employee's
ability to perform their role or creates a hostile environment for
colleagues, at HR's discretion.
- Contractors are held to the confidentiality and harassment provisions
of this policy but are not subject to the tiered warning system -
violations by contractors are handled through contract termination
directly.

This document covers what business expenses are reimbursable, approval
limits by role, and submission deadlines.

- Reimbursable expenses include: client meals, business travel
(see Travel Policy for per-diem details), software subscriptions
approved for the employee's role, and home office supplies up to
$150/year.
- All expenses must be submitted through the finance portal within
30 days of the purchase date. Expenses submitted after 30 days require
Director approval to be processed, and are not guaranteed reimbursement.
- Expenses require manager approval before reimbursement is issued.
Approval limits by role are as follows:  
| Role     | Approval limit (per expense)  |
|----------|-------------------------------|
| Manager  | $1,000                        |
| Director | $5,000                        |
| VP       | $25,000                       |  
- Any single expense exceeding a role's approval limit must be escalated
to the next level up, in addition to the employee's direct manager.
- Personal expenses (e.g. entertainment unrelated to client work,
personal phone bills) are not reimbursable under any circumstance.

- Expenses related to conferences or training require pre-approval from
the employee's manager *before* the purchase is made, unlike other
categories which are approved after the fact.
- Contractors follow a separate reimbursement process defined in their
individual agreements and are not covered by the approval limits table
above.
- If an expense report includes a mix of reimbursable and
non-reimbursable items, only the reimbursable portion is processed;
the report is not rejected in full unless more than 50% of the total
amount is non-reimbursable.

This document covers device usage, password requirements, and access
control for company systems.

- All company-issued devices must have full-disk encryption and
automatic screen lock (5 minutes of inactivity) enabled at all times.
- Passwords must be at least 12 characters, rotated every 90 days, and
may not be reused within the last 5 password cycles. Multi-factor
authentication is required for all systems handling client data.
- Production system access is granted on a role basis and reviewed
quarterly. See the Access Control Policy for the full approval
workflow and role-to-permission mapping.
- Employees working internationally for more than 30 consecutive days
(see Remote Work Policy) must use company-approved VPN software at all
times when accessing internal systems, regardless of the destination
country's data regulations.
- Personal devices may access email and calendar only, never production
systems or client data, under any circumstance.

- Contractors are issued time-limited access credentials that expire
automatically at the end of their contract term, rather than following
the quarterly review cycle that applies to employees.
- A lost or stolen device must be reported to IT within 2 hours of
discovery. Failure to report within 24 hours is treated as a Moderate
violation under the Code of Conduct, regardless of whether any data
was actually compromised.
- Emergency production access outside the normal quarterly review
process may be granted for up to 24 hours by a Director, but must be
retroactively documented and reviewed within 48 hours.

This document covers the first-week checklist, probation period terms,
and role classification for new hires.

- All new hires undergo a 90-day probation period, during which either
party may terminate employment with 5 business days' notice, without
the standard notice period described in the Termination & Resignation
Policy.
- Roles are classified at time of hire as either "office-required" or
"remote-eligible" - this classification determines Remote Work Policy
eligibility once probation ends.
- New hires receive company equipment (laptop, access badge, required
software licenses) before their start date whenever logistically
possible, and no later than end of day on day 1.
- A 30-60-90 day check-in is scheduled with the employee's manager and
an HR representative, to review progress against onboarding goals.
- New hires are not eligible to use PTO during their first 30 days (see
PTO / Vacation Policy), but do begin accruing PTO and sick leave from
their start date.

- Employees transferring internally from another team or role do not
undergo a new 90-day probation period, unless the transfer includes a
change from individual contributor to a people-management role.
- If a new hire's start date falls within the last two weeks of a fiscal
quarter (the PTO blackout period), the 90-day probation clock still
starts on their actual start date and is not delayed.
- Contractors converting to full-time employment retain their prior
tenure for PTO accrual-tier purposes (see PTO / Vacation Policy) only
if the conversion happens within 30 days of the contract ending;
otherwise tenure resets to zero.

This document covers leave eligibility and duration for childbirth,
adoption, and foster placement, for all parenting roles.

- Employees with 6+ months of continuous employment are eligible for
parental leave. Employees with less than 6 months of tenure are only
eligible for unpaid leave under this policy, unless local law requires
otherwise.
- Birthing parents receive 16 weeks of fully paid leave. Non-birthing
parents (including in cases of adoption or foster placement) receive
8 weeks of fully paid leave.
- Leave may be taken continuously or split into two blocks within the
first 12 months following the birth or placement, but not split into
more than two blocks without HR approval.
- Parental leave accrual-pause rules for PTO follow the same 90-day
threshold described in the PTO / Vacation Policy.

- In the case of multiple births (twins, triplets, etc.), leave duration
is not extended beyond the standard 16/8 week allowance, except when
a documented medical complication requires additional recovery time -
in that case, the excess is covered under Sick Leave & Medical Policy
provisions, not parental leave.
- Employees who separate from the company within 6 months of returning
from parental leave are not required to repay any portion of the paid
leave received, unlike some signing bonuses or relocation packages.
- Same-sex couples and domestic partners are eligible under the same
terms as married couples; eligibility is not contingent on legal
marital status.

This document covers pay schedules, overtime calculation, and bonus
structures for all employees.

- Employees are paid on a bi-weekly schedule, every other Friday. If a
payday falls on a public holiday, payment is issued the preceding
business day.
- Non-exempt employees (hourly-classified roles) are paid overtime at
1.5x their base hourly rate for any hours worked beyond 40 in a single
week. Exempt (salaried) employees are not eligible for overtime pay
under any circumstance.
- Annual performance bonuses are calculated as a percentage of base
salary, tied to the employee's most recent Performance Review Policy
rating:
- "Exceeds expectations": up to 15% of base salary
- "Meets expectations": up to 8% of base salary
- "Below expectations": not eligible for bonus that cycle
- Salary reviews occur annually, aligned with the performance review
cycle. Off-cycle salary adjustments require VP approval and are
reserved for role changes or retention cases.

- Employees who transfer between exempt and non-exempt classification
mid-pay-period have their pay for that period calculated on a
split basis - the exempt portion and non-exempt (with overtime, if
applicable) portion are calculated separately, not averaged.
- New hires starting mid-pay-period receive a prorated first paycheck
based on actual days worked, not a full period's pay.
- Bonus eligibility requires the employee to be actively employed on the
bonus payout date, except in the case of an approved medical or
parental leave (see Parental Leave Policy), where eligibility is
preserved.

This document covers review frequency, rating criteria, and how ratings
connect to compensation and other policies.

- Formal performance reviews occur annually, aligned with the
Payroll & Compensation Policy salary review cycle. New hires receive
an additional informal review at the 90-day probation mark.
- Ratings fall into three tiers: "Exceeds expectations," "Meets
expectations," and "Below expectations." Ratings are determined by the
employee's direct manager, with input from at least one peer reviewer
for roles at Director level or above.
- Employees rated "Below expectations" are placed on a formal 60-day
improvement plan. Failure to show documented improvement by the end of
the 60 days may result in termination under the Termination &
Resignation Policy.
- Review ratings directly determine annual bonus eligibility, as
described in the Payroll & Compensation Policy, and may affect Remote
Work Policy eligibility at manager discretion.

- An employee may formally dispute a rating within 10 business days of
receiving it. During an active dispute, no policy consequence tied to
that rating (bonus reduction, remote work suspension) takes effect
until the dispute is resolved.
- Employees on an approved leave of absence during the review period
(medical, parental, etc.) have their review postponed until 30 days
after their return, rather than being rated based on a partial year.
- Peer reviewer feedback is considered advisory only for
Director-level-and-above reviews - the final rating decision always
rests with the employee's direct manager, not the peer reviewer.

This document covers paid time off (PTO) accrual, usage, carryover, and
payout rules for all full-time employees at Northwind Analytics.

- Full-time employees accrue PTO based on tenure:
- 0–2 years: 15 days per year
- 2–5 years: 20 days per year
- 5+ years: 25 days per year
- PTO accrues monthly (e.g. an employee with 15 days/year accrues 1.25
days per month), not in a lump sum at the start of the year.
- Part-time employees (working 20–29 hours/week) accrue PTO on a
pro-rated basis, proportional to hours worked relative to a 40-hour
work week.
- Employees must submit PTO requests through the HR portal at least
5 business days in advance for absences of 3 or more consecutive days.
- Requests for 1–2 days off require at least 48 hours advance notice.
- Manager approval is required for all PTO requests. Managers must
respond within 3 business days; if no response is given, the request
is automatically approved.
- PTO cannot be taken during a company-wide blackout period (the last
two weeks of each fiscal quarter), except for emergencies approved by
HR directly.

- Up to 5 unused PTO days may be carried over into the following
calendar year. Any unused days beyond that cap are forfeited on
December 31st, unless local labor law requires otherwise.
- Employees in jurisdictions where forfeiture is not legally permitted
will instead receive a cash payout for unused days beyond the
5-day carryover cap, calculated at their current daily pay rate.
- Upon resignation or termination, employees are paid out for all
accrued, unused PTO, regardless of the reason for separation.

- Employees on an approved leave of absence (medical, parental, etc.)
continue to accrue PTO during the first 90 days of leave only. Accrual
pauses after 90 days and resumes upon return to active work.
- New hires may not use PTO during their first 30 days of employment,
even if they have accrued a partial day, except in the case of a
documented medical emergency.
- If a public holiday falls within an approved PTO period, that day is
not deducted from the employee's PTO balance.
- Employees who transfer between full-time and part-time status mid-year
have their accrual rate recalculated prospectively from the date of
the change; past accrual is not retroactively adjusted.

This document covers eligibility, equipment, and expectations for
employees working remotely, either fully remote or in a hybrid
arrangement.

- Employees are eligible for hybrid work (up to 3 days/week remote)
after completing their 90-day probation period, unless their role is
designated as office-required (see Onboarding Process for role
classifications).
- Fully remote arrangements require Director-level approval and are
reviewed annually.
- Remote employees must be available during a 4-hour "core overlap
window" aligned with their team's primary timezone, even if their
full schedule is flexible outside that window.
- Company-issued equipment (laptop, monitor, headset) is provided for
all remote employees. A one-time home office stipend of $500 is
available within the first 60 days of a remote arrangement being
approved.
- Employees working from a different country than their contract's
country of record for more than 30 consecutive days must notify HR in
advance, due to tax and legal implications - see the IT & Security
Policy for device compliance requirements when working
internationally.

- Contractors are not eligible for the home office stipend, regardless
of remote work arrangement, except when explicitly stated in their
individual contract.
- Employees may work remotely from a non-primary location (e.g. while
traveling) for up to 10 business days per year without formal
approval, unless the destination requires the international-work
notification described above.
- An employee whose performance rating falls below "meets expectations"
(see Performance Review Policy) may have remote eligibility suspended
at manager discretion until the next review cycle, except when the
rating is under formal dispute.

This document covers paid sick leave, medical certification
requirements, and extended medical leave, separate from PTO.

- Full-time employees receive 10 paid sick days per calendar year,
separate from PTO balance (see PTO / Vacation Policy). Sick days do
not accrue monthly - the full 10 days are available starting January
1st, or on the employee's start date if hired mid-year (pro-rated).
- A medical certificate is required for any sick leave of 3 or more
consecutive days. For 1-2 day absences, a manager notification is
sufficient - no certificate is required.
- Unused sick days do not carry over to the following year and are not
paid out upon resignation or termination, unlike PTO.
- Extended medical leave (beyond the 10-day sick leave allowance)
requires a formal leave of absence request through HR, and follows the
accrual-pause rules described in the PTO / Vacation Policy for
leaves beyond 90 days.

- Sick days used for a dependent's medical needs (child, spouse, or
registered domestic partner) are covered under this same policy, up to
5 of the 10 annual days, unless local law provides broader family
leave coverage.
- An employee who exhausts their 10 sick days may draw from their PTO
balance instead, at their discretion, without needing separate
approval - this is the one case where sick leave and PTO balances are
interchangeable.
- Sick leave taken during an already-approved PTO period does not
convert that day back to PTO, except when a medical certificate is
provided within 5 business days of returning to work.

This document covers notice periods, final pay, and offboarding
requirements for voluntary and involuntary separations.

- Employees resigning voluntarily must provide 2 weeks' written notice
for individual contributor roles, and 4 weeks' notice for Manager
level and above, submitted to their direct manager and HR.
- Involuntary termination for performance reasons requires completion of
the improvement plan process described in the Performance Review
Policy, except in cases of a Severe violation under the Code of
Conduct, which allows for immediate termination without a prior
improvement plan.
- Final pay, including any accrued and unused PTO (see PTO / Vacation
Policy), is issued within 5 business days of the separation date,
or sooner if required by local law.
- All company equipment (laptop, access badge, phone) must be returned
on or before the last working day. Failure to return equipment within
10 business days may result in its cost being deducted from final pay,
where legally permitted.

- Employees terminated during their 90-day probation period (see
Onboarding Process) are not subject to the standard notice period
requirements in either direction.
- An employee who resigns and later requests to rescind that resignation
may do so only with manager approval, and only before the resignation
has been formally processed by HR - once processed, rescission is
treated as a new hire application.
- Unused sick leave is not paid out upon separation, per the Sick Leave
& Medical Policy, regardless of the reason for termination or
resignation - this is a key contrast with PTO payout treatment.

This document covers trip approval, per-diem rates, and flight/hotel
booking rules for business travel.

- All business travel requires manager pre-approval before booking,
regardless of cost - unlike standard expenses (see Expense
Reimbursement Policy), which are approved after the fact.
- Domestic per-diem for meals not covered by a client or event is $75/day.
International per-diem is $110/day, adjusted by finance for
high-cost-of-living destinations on a case-by-case basis.
- Flight class eligibility is based on role and flight duration:  
| Role                   | Flights under 6 hours  | Flights 6+ hours  |
|------------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| Individual Contributor | Economy                | Economy           |
| Manager                | Economy                | Premium Economy   |
| Director and above     | Premium Economy        | Business          |  
- Hotel bookings should not exceed $250/night domestically or
$350/night internationally, without Director approval for the excess.

- Employees may use personal frequent flyer miles or hotel loyalty
points for business travel and are not required to disclose or
surrender any rewards earned, even though the company paid for the
ticket or stay.
- Travel extended for personal reasons (e.g. staying an extra weekend)
is permitted, but any additional cost - including per-diem for the
extended days - is the employee's responsibility, not the company's.
- In the case of a trip cancellation due to a documented medical
emergency (see Sick Leave & Medical Policy), non-refundable booking
costs are covered by the company and do not count against the
employee's expense approval limit described in the Expense
Reimbursement Policy.
